visualReview.notes: Inspected the lit view on the original mountainous field, four turntables and five detail views. The tiled wings preserve the site outline and two open courts, with an octagonal end, a domed basilica and the separate high two-bay campanile. In the courts the revised gallery paving closes the floor around the piers.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected ten dated viewer frames on the placement fixture, showing shared tile, rubble wall, cut stone, wood and paving materials. The geographic placement loaded and unloaded successfully. Terrain was checked separately in the source-based review.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected 26 current frames, including four authored levels and their transitions. Skyline retains the plan, courtyard openings, octagonal museum end, church domes and detached belfry. Street and closeup add open arch reveals, stone piers, paving, timber rails and the courtyard well.

geographicReview.notes: The named monastery node and native compound envelope, principal court, church, belfry and museum polygons locate the structure. The connected wings step toward higher natural terrain. Inspected the original unmasked field and the compound at grade. Precise terrace and floor elevations are approximate.

fidelityReview.scope: The principal Kykkos Monastery compound on the Troodos mountainside, including the arcaded courts, main church, campanile and adjoining museum range, in its 2009 documented appearance.
fidelityReview.notes: The cleared courtyard photos establish round and pointed gallery openings, rubble-stone walls, dark rails, a pale well surround, and low tiled roofs. A cleared third view supplies the twin bell openings, crosses and domed foreground belfry. Footprints and the visitor guide corroborate the domed basilica and freestanding hillside bell tower. The lower court plan, roof junctions, facade rhythm, floor levels and heights are estimates.

imageryReview.notes: The three Qualla photographs match the published native Wikimedia originals by checksum, with own-work public-domain dedication by photographer Olavfin. The photographed modern mosaic was excluded. Materials use shared procedural graphs and vertex color without embedded photographs.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: Kykkos Monastery, its two arcaded courts, domed church, museum range and 1882 hillside campanile in its 2009 appearance.

limitations: Building envelopes follow the native mapped monastery, church, paved court, independent belfry and octagonal museum end. The lower well court is an estimate within the mapped envelope.

Staff and visitor rooms, roof heights and pitches, belfry and dome sections, approximate courtyard levels and patterns of exterior openings are inferred from public-domain reference photographs, the visitor guide and the original elevation samples.
Only the architecture is modeled. Wall painting, mosaic designs, objects in the museum and church interiors are absent.
The original Copernicus field is unmodified. Its roughly 30 m horizontal sampling cannot resolve steps, finished paving, adjacent terrain cuts and small retaining walls.
